items.question: What is refraction?
items.expectedAnswer: The bending of light as it changes speed crossing a boundary between media.
items.explanation: Refraction is the change in direction of light due to a change in speed at a boundary.
options: The bending of light as it changes speed crossing a boundary between media.
The bouncing of light off a surface.
The splitting of light into colours only.

items.question: From where is the angle of incidence measured?
items.expectedAnswer: From the normal (the line perpendicular to the surface).
items.explanation: Angles in optics are measured from the normal, not the surface.
options: From the normal (the line perpendicular to the surface).

items.question: How is refractive index defined?
items.expectedAnswer: n = c/v (speed of light in vacuum ÷ speed in the medium).
items.explanation: Refractive index n = c/v; it is always ≥ 1.
options: n = c/v (speed of light in vacuum ÷ speed in the medium).

items.question: When light passes from air into glass (a denser medium), it bends...
items.explanation: Entering a denser (slower) medium, light bends towards the normal.

items.question: When light passes from glass into air (a less dense medium), it bends...
items.explanation: Entering a less dense (faster) medium, light bends away from the normal.

items.question: Which equation is Snell's Law?
items.explanation: Snell's Law: n₁sinθ₁ = n₂sinθ₂.

items.question: A medium has a refractive index greater than 1. This means light travels...
items.expectedAnswer: slower in the medium than in a vacuum.
items.explanation: n = c/v > 1 means v < c, so light is slower in the medium.
options: slower in the medium than in a vacuum.
faster in the medium than in a vacuum.
at the same speed as in a vacuum.

items.question: Light in a vacuum has refractive index...
items.explanation: In a vacuum n = c/c = 1.

items.question: If light hits a boundary along the normal (angle of incidence 0°), what happens?
items.expectedAnswer: It passes straight through without bending.
items.explanation: At 0° incidence there is no bending; light continues straight (though its speed changes).
options: It passes straight through without bending.

items.question: The speed of light in glass is 2×10⁸ m·s⁻¹. What is the refractive index of the glass? (c = 3×10⁸ m·s⁻¹)
Light travels from air (n = 1) into water (n = 1.33) at an angle of incidence of 30°. Find the angle of refraction. (sin30° = 0.5)
items.explanation: n₁sinθ₁ = n₂sinθ₂ ⇒ sinθ₂ = (1 × 0.5)/1.33 = 0.376 ⇒ θ₂ = 22.1°.

items.question: Light goes from glass (n = 1.5) into air (n = 1) at an angle of incidence of 20°. Find the angle of refraction. (sin20° = 0.342)
items.explanation: sinθ₂ = (1.5 × 0.342)/1 = 0.513 ⇒ θ₂ = 30.9° (bends away from the normal).

items.question: Why does a straw in a glass of water appear bent at the surface?
items.expectedAnswer: Light from the straw refracts as it leaves the water, changing direction.
items.explanation: Light bends (refracts) at the water-air boundary, making the submerged part appear displaced.
options: Light from the straw refracts as it leaves the water, changing direction.
The straw physically bends in water.

items.question: A ray enters a medium and bends towards the normal. What can you conclude about the second medium?
items.expectedAnswer: It is denser (higher refractive index) than the first.
items.explanation: Bending towards the normal means entering a denser, slower medium (higher n).
options: It is less dense than the first.
It is denser (higher refractive index) than the first.
It has the same density as the first.

items.question: The refractive index of a diamond is 2.42. What is the speed of light in diamond? (c = 3×10⁸ m·s⁻¹)
Light travels from medium A (n = 1.2) to medium B (n = 1.6). Compared with medium A, the light in medium B is...
items.expectedAnswer: slower and bends towards the normal.
items.explanation: Higher n in B means slower light, bending towards the normal.
options: slower and bends towards the normal.
faster and bends away from the normal.

items.question: Light passes from water (n = 1.33) into air (n = 1.00) at 25° incidence. sin25° = 0.423. Find the angle of refraction.
Does the frequency of light change when it refracts into a new medium?
items.expectedAnswer: No — frequency stays the same; speed and wavelength change.
items.explanation: On refraction frequency is unchanged; the speed and wavelength change together (v = fλ).
options: No — frequency stays the same; speed and wavelength change.

items.question: A ray hits a glass surface and part of it changes direction on entering. The bending happens because...
items.expectedAnswer: the light changes speed at the boundary.
items.explanation: Refraction (bending) is caused by the change in light's speed crossing the boundary.
options: the light changes speed at the boundary.
the glass absorbs part of the light.

items.question: Two media have refractive indices 1.0 and 1.5. In which is the speed of light greater?
items.explanation: Lower n means higher speed (v = c/n), so light is faster where n = 1.0.
options: The speed is equal in both.
